items.q: What is "your metabolism" in Rutter's frame?
items.a: Not a single furnace. Organismal calories-in/out is the **sum of ~30 trillion cell maps**. Each cell takes nutrients, runs its chemistry, and returns waste — a **constellation of metabolisms**, not one rate.
After glycolysis, pyruvate is **burned** in mitochondria for ATP + CO₂, or kept as **biomass** (new cell, repair, antibodies). Lumber for **heat** vs lumber for the **house**.

The **mitochondrial pyruvate carrier** — the hole that lets pyruvate in so it can be oxidized. Inferred for **60–70 years**; identified **~2012** (Rutter/Thummel + Martinou). Whole-body knockout dies around **embryonic day 12–13**.

items.q: Why do heart-specific MPC knockout mice die of heart failure?
items.a: Not ATP bankruptcy — they still **burn fat**. Glucose is misallocated into **growth**. Cardiomyocytes that should **be heart** start **making more heart**; the pump **dilates**.

It is a **metabolic omnivore**: fat, glucose, lactate, ketones, amino acids. About **70–80%** of cardiac energy comes from **fat**, especially when fasted. Glucagon tells fat cells to **release**; the heart is a destination that must not shut down.

items.q: Is lactate just the burn you feel in exercise?
items.a: No. It is pyruvate's **other fate** — a **biomass mediator** and a real **fuel** (the heart consumes it). "Waste product" was a label that shut down discovery. Excess still kills (**lactic acidosis**).

items.q: Did Warburg prove mitochondria in cancer are broken?
items.a: He observed **low oxygen consumption**. The old inference was **broken mitochondria cause cancer**. Rutter: low O₂ is a **surrogate for build-not-burn**. Cancer mitochondria are often **very good at making stuff**. FDG-PET lights tumors because they take glucose to **build**.

items.q: What cancer-therapy future does he sketch?
items.a: **Combination** hits on that tumor's mutations **and** metabolic program — like **HIV triple therapy** — because a **0.1%** resistant clone can repopulate. Classify by **phenotype**, not only breast/liver/colon **address**.

items.q: How can extra calories hurt below the waistline?
items.a: Mitochondria **overpowered** before ATP conversion leak **reactive oxygen species** that damage DNA and proteins — a candidate **aging** mechanism. Free fatty acids are **acutely** toxic; high glucose is **chronically** damaging (minutes vs years).
